comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — bonjour-dv.ru's fixed blue cookie-consent banner covers the product page content; it is hidden by adding bonjour-dv.ru to the existing shared rule `##.fixed.bottom-0` at AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt line 171 (under the comment `! ##.fixed.bottom-0`), which apply_rule verified with the banner gone and page integrity intact. ## Rule `bonjour-dv.ru##.fixed.bottom-0` ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie-consent notice annoyance, which the repository's Annoyances/Cookie Notices filter covers; it is not a paywall, not an anti-adblock wall, not self-promotion and not a scam page, so no policy rule closes it. <!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"2947e38f7434f74392415a281bbaf434bec9e4d8b5b270184eb05badc9c5ac7e"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — myupload.us/d/5r5stJm4q2 redirects to watchnow7.space, whose Interstitial module hides the download control behind a "Please disable your ad blocker" alert driven by detectAdBlock():⁠ a bait div plus a HEAD fetch of pagead2.googlesyndication.com/pagead/js/adsbygoogle.js. That alert could not be reproduced (the server sends antiAdblock:⁠false for this traffic) and apply_rule refused every session with cli_route_session_required, so the candidate stays unverified:⁠ add watchnow7.space to the shared prevent-fetch rule under the comment at BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt line 82 (line 83 group) rather than hiding the alert, which replaces the only download control.

## Candidate for review

`watchnow7.space#%#//scriptlet('prevent-fetch', 'pagead2.googlesyndication.com')`

BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt

Not verified: apply_rule never ran:⁠ every call returned validationSkipped:⁠true, errorKind cli_route_session_required, requiredAction launch_cli_evidence_browser, for extension:⁠none and extension:⁠prepared sessions alike, and no advertised tool yields that session, so no before/after phase or vision review exists. Independently, the reporter-defined alert could not be observed in any phase because the site's server sends "antiAdblock":⁠false with an empty ads array for this traffic, and detectAdBlock() only runs when that server prop is true; the reporter settings import also returned settingsVerified:⁠false. A maintainer should merge watchnow7.space into the existing shared rule on line 83 under the comment '! #⁠%#⁠//scriptlet('prevent-fetch', 'pagead2.googlesyndication.com')' (line 82 of the same file) instead of adding this duplicate line, and should confirm the fix on a mobile AdGuard for Android client, where the site enables the check.

## Missing information

- apply_rule cannot obtain a CLI evidence browser session in this run: Every apply_rule call was refused with validationSkipped:⁠true, errorKind "cli_route_session_required", requiredAction "launch_cli_evidence_browser" (two candidate attempts spent, remainingCandidateAttempts 2 then 1). Sessions launched with extension:⁠"none" (desktop, targetUrl myupload.us and watchnow7.space) and sessions launched with extension:⁠"prepared" (settings kind reported_on_current with the issue's Android import URL, and settings kind agent_selected filterIds 2,3,4,11,17, stealthEnabled true) were all refused the same way, although their get_applied_rules reported engine "AdGuard CLI" and the local.adguard.org content-script request. No advertised tool produces the "cli_evidence_browser" session the validator demands, so no candidate could be validated in this environment. Separately, the launch with the issue's reporter settings import URL returned settingsVerified:⁠false, so even reporter-profile parity could not be established.

comment.body:
<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"dba75f502cd837b8a4844dc903def628fa0a8cde6c1ef9cb07c6ca5af0659fed"} -->
The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — I could not reproduce the reported ad on www⁠.maxon.net/en/downloads with the reporter's own Base+Tracking baseline:⁠ the reported text "Log in and download the Maxon app." appears nowhere in the page HTML (also checked /en and /en/sale), et.maxon.net made no request among 469 HAR entries, no ad loader or overlay is present, and 30 s of waiting/scroll produced no popup. The only ad-like element is the site's own "CYBER SALE" promo bar, which is first-party self-promotion and does not match the report, so I recommend closing as not reproduced instead of substituting a rule for it.

## Policy rationale

The run instruction's filter policy states no rule that closes this report:⁠ it is not a paywall, not an anti-adblock wall, and not a scam/phishing case, so rule generation is not blocked. Closing is recommended on reproduction grounds only:⁠ the reported ad element and the reported tracker host are absent from the successfully loaded reported page in every session and page variant examined.

## Missing information

- Reported ad cannot be located:⁠ issue body carries no element selector or usable screenshot: Issue #⁠248286 identifies its target only by free text ("tracker:⁠ et.maxon.net" and "Log in and download the Maxon app."); its attached screenshot renders as a uniform blank white image with no annotation (analyze_screenshot index 1:⁠ pageObstruction error_or_blank, no target). No element selector, bounding box, or annotation tells which page element is meant, so the reported element could neither be located on the live page nor matched to a candidate rule. If the reporting wizard captured an element, that data is absent from the issue body.

## Artifacts

Indeterminate — niganpro.com serves a first-party "CHP Ads Block Detector" anti-adblock gate ('Ads Blocker Detected!!!' + CHPADBLOCK badge), whose wrapper matches the existing shared element-hiding family in BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt, but in the Chromium/AdGuard CLI baseline the wrapper computes display:⁠none from the site's own CSS and never becomes visible, so apply_rule ended with baseline_symptom_absent and no rule could be validated. comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — amj30.com's homepage opens two self-owned modal popups (the reporter's "请务必牢记回家地址" alternate-domain notice and a "站点公告" notice) that dim the page and lock scrolling; blocking the routing script or stubbing showModal failed because the site falls back to the open attribute. Aborting reads of HTMLDialogElement.prototype.showModal suppressed both popups with the page left intact in the validated experiment. ## Rule `amj30.com#%#//scriptlet('abort-on-property-read', 'HTMLDialogElement.prototype.showModal')` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale Run instruction:⁠ the site's own advertising (self-promotion, elements in which the site promotes its own products and services) gets a rule in AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt; whether it is annoying enough to block is the maintainer's call. The reported symptom is not a paywall, not an anti-adblock wall and not a scam page, so none of the instruction's close-or-hand-off rules applies. No rule is closed by the maintainer rules either:⁠ the popup is neutralized with a scriptlet only because hiding is not enough (the dialogs are modal and keep the page scroll-locked), which matches the maintainers' anti-popup guidance. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/baceba8687936f419bf0892897614529a43aaccd/AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt) Under the heading `! SECTION: Self-promo - Regular rules`, before [line 232](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/baceba8687936f419bf0892897614529a43aaccd/AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt#L232). ## Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — cpmclic.io hides a honeypot div (classes ad-banner ad-zone adsense sponsored-ad) that AdGuard Base already hides via #⁠#⁠.sponsored-ad, so its inline detector shows a full-viewport "turn off / remove your adblock extension" wall whose only button reloads the page. Adding cpmclic.io#⁠@⁠#⁠.sponsored-ad beside the existing #⁠@⁠#⁠.sponsored-ad exceptions in BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt defeated the detector in apply_rule (phase C antiAdblockDetected false, wall gone, page integrity intact). ## Rule `cpmclic.io#@#.sponsored-ad` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The filter policy blocks anti-adblock walls that aggressively insist on disabling or removing the ad blocker or effectively prevent using the website; this overlay covers the entire viewport, offers no alternative to disabling filtering and its only control reloads the page into the same wall. The run instruction's anti-adblock gate is met in substance:⁠ the detector logic was read from the page and rides in the captured first-party document request GET https:⁠//cpmclic.io/6IbwaH (document, 200); no separate detector request exists on this site. No policy exclusion applies:⁠ this is not a paywall, not the site's own self-promotion, and not a scam/phishing page. The reporter used uBlock Origin on Firefox Mobile rather than an AdGuard product; the instruction does not make the reporting product a policy bar, and the proposed rule is standard element-hiding-exception syntax shared by both blockers (recorded as a parity gap, not as a block). ## Place in the list [BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/d597878cf646da13c248d38d53db6d8886362343/BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt) At the end of the file: BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt has no sorted region; it keeps per-issue blocks (an issue-link comment followed by that site's rules) appended in the file, and the reported site has no block there yet, so a new block belongs at the end. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/45942354978 Automated analysis against filters at `d597878`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"c2b9259427e0acc5db2afca36702ca70c51b8fc864103543dadbd72ce2435e53"} -->
The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — Under the prepared AdGuard CLI baseline, https:⁠//dungeon.report/ loads fully (HTTP 200, 35 requests, 0 blocked, 18/18 images, no rule hiding anything) and the reported "can't reach this page / ERR_FAILED" state never appears; no rule in this repository mentions dungeon.report, and the issue's own AdGuard-disabled screenshot shows the same error, so filtering is not shown to cause it. Recommending close:⁠ no rule is needed for this report.

## Policy rationale

No repository policy rule blocks rule generation for this report:⁠ it is not a paywall, not an anti-adblock wall (no detector script exists to gate anything), and not a self-promotion case. The reported defect is simply absent under filtering, so there is nothing for a rule to fix; the recommendation to close is for a maintainer to confirm, as the run instruction reserves the close decision to maintainers. Filter policy on incorrect blocking (whole-document policy document, cited) asks a dispute to name the blocking rule behind the breakage; no repository rule matches dungeon.report at all, and the live filtered run blocked nothing.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/45941992638

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reporter's "fake buttons" on epicroms.net are three purple `button.file-download-btnn` "Direct Download" controls with no href and no data-download-url (clicking them does nothing), while the real ROM download is `#game-downloads-1790 a.download-button`. `epicroms.net##.file-download-btnn` was verified in the AdGuard baseline (3/3 hidden, page intact, no residue) and belongs at BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt:⁠1448, next to the existing `game-repack.site##.file-download-btnn`, whose domain list the maintainer can extend instead. ## Rule `epicroms.net##.file-download-btnn` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The reported element is an ad-styled fake download placement, and the instruction's filter policy gives ads a rule like any other ad wherever they are served from; it is not a paywall, not an anti-adblock wall and not a cookie-consent problem, so none of the policy clauses that close a report applies. The repository already hides the same selector on another site (game-repack.site#⁠#⁠.file-download-btnn, BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt:⁠1448), so the rule kind and list match established practice. The candidate was fully validated in the locked browser_extension baseline (verified experiment and vision review, symptom resolved, page intact, no residue), so the propose-rule outcome applies rather than a close or analysis-only one. ## Place in the list [BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/ff0513048ff30f9d36f972c5319d95b8d536a8ff/BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt) Under the heading `! NOTE: Specific rules`, before [line 1448](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/ff0513048ff30f9d36f972c5319d95b8d536a8ff/BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt#L1448). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Not reproduced — The reported pop-under tabs (pucksdopes.qpon, dyeingasprelaw.cfd) never appeared on the loaded homepage:⁠ after clicks and waits, both the unfiltered control and the reporter's filter profile opened zero popup tabs and full-page vision found no interstitial. Base filter already blocks the exact ad requests named in the reporter's ESET screenshots, so I recommend closing as not reproduced.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Policy rationale

The run instruction's filter policy states that ads for other companies get a rule like any other ad, so nothing here blocks rule generation. No policy exception applies:⁠ this is not a paywall, not an anti-adblock wall, not self-promotion and not a scam/phishing page. The report nevertheless carries no reproducible defect to fix, so the outcome is a recommended close rather than a rule.

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The VirusTotal file report shows the self-promo link "Do you want to automate checks?" in the "Security vendors' analysis" header slot; it is rendered inside shadow DOM, so the existing self-promo rules (which anchor on developers.virustotal.com) no longer match and a `hide-in-shadow-dom` scriptlet with the current docs.virustotal.com link is needed. The verified rule was added to the existing virustotal.com group of AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt; a maintainer may prefer to fold it into lines 4735-4736 of that file, since the `.alert-info` part already exists there. ## Rule `virustotal.com#%#//scriptlet('hide-in-shadow-dom', 'span[slot="header"] > div + a[href^="https://docs.virustotal.com/"], .alert-info')` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The run instruction routes the site's own self-promotion to AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt and leaves the annoying-enough call to the maintainer. This is VirusTotal promoting its own paid API (no third party paying for it), served by the site itself, so the self-promotion rule applies. No paywall, anti-adblock wall, or non-website-filtering product issue is involved. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/b6269c4f81389374d3897595554504e5a4dbc0e2/AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt) Before [line 4737](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/b6269c4f81389374d3897595554504e5a4dbc0e2/AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt#L4737). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/45977892843 Automated analysis against filters at `b6269c4`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

comment.body: Regarding the rules for `.ad-native-campaign-leftout` (the first and the last ones), not all the items are ad or native ad. E.g. currently `https://www.famitsu.com/article/202611/94840` is a normal article. I guess it's safer to target only items linked to Amazon. We probably can't distinguish native ads, so maybe it's okay to hide them all in the Annoyances list; i.e. move the first and the last rule to self-promotion, but for JPF add a new rule to target only the item with `[href^="https://amzn.asia"]`.

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — baku.ws fills its in-article ad slot (Global Promo GP-29, the banner the reporter outlined) from the third-party vendor loader media.globalpromo.az/placements.js, and this repository has no rule for that vendor. The banner never rendered in the locked adguard_cli baseline (all seven [⁠data-gp-slot]⁠ containers were empty) and apply_rule refused the blocking candidate twice with baseline_symptom_absent, so the rule could not be verified and is handed to a maintainer.

## Candidate for review

`||globalpromo.az^$domain=baku.ws`

BaseFilter/sections/foreign.txt

Not verified: apply_rule refused the candidate twice with baseline_symptom_absent (second run retryable:⁠false, requiredAction finish_fix_analysis_only):⁠ the reported MOKA LAND banner in the Global Promo GP-29 slot could not be distinguished between the unfiltered phase A and the filtered baseline B, and the harness stated the filtered baseline made no allowed request to globalpromo.az, so a block of that host had nothing to stop. Full-page vision of the locked baseline likewise found no banner (all seven [⁠data-gp-slot]⁠ containers empty, height 0), the two media.globalpromo.az requests ended with responseStatus 0, and no applied rule was attributed to that block (3 x ERR_BLOCKED_BY_RESPONSE.NotSameOrigin in console), so neither the ad's rendering nor the candidate's effect could be validated in this environment.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/45996785615

# Sorry. The website is infected by AdShield, Inc.

Unfortunately, It is complicated to resolve with a regular adblock rule because the website is being protected by service of Ad-Shield that is an anti-adblock company.

## Userscript Installation
Please block Ad-Shield advertisement by installing [tinyShield userscript](https://github.com/List-KR/tinyShield).
Please check its installation guideline written in English by visiting [this URL](https://github.com/List-KR/tinyShield/blob/main/README.md).

If you can understand Korean language, please refer https://github.com/List-KR/tinyShield/blob/main/README.ko.md.

<details>
<summary>Detailed description for iOS users</summary>

1. Install [**Usercripts**](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/userscripts/id1463298887) app
2. Enable **Usercripts** extension in Safari settings
	* iOS 18+: `System settings` => `Apps` => `Safari` => `Extensions`
	* iOS 17 and older: `System settings` => `Safari` => `Extensions`
	Find **Usercripts**, enable it and allow `On other sites` permission
4. Open the [tinyShield ](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@list-kr/tinyshield@latest/dist/tinyShield.user.js) userscript URL in browser
5. Press the extensions icon in the address bar of Safari and select Userscripts 
6. Tap to install
7. In opened popup, scroll down and press Install button
8. Done.

</details>

## Still Have a Problem?
An issue is occurred when the userscript is applied, please report to [this issue tracker](https://github.com/List-KR/tinyShield/issues).

issue.title: 39macvartv.live
issue.body:
### Issue URL (Ads) [https://39macvartv.live/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2F39macvartv.live%2F) ### Comment > ## Summary > `39macvartv.live` has a rotating domain. The site's own header says the next domain will be the same name with the number +1 (40macvartv.live, ...). With the AdGuard Turkish filter on, the "Mr. Bahis" betting ads are still visible. > > ## What's left > | Where | What | Element | > |---|---|---| > | Top bar | Mr. Bahis social links (`heylink.me/mrbahissosyal`) | `.header-top` | > | Header | Mr. Bahis logo (`logo.png`) | `header .logo` | > | Footer | Mr. Bahis logo again | `footer img[src$="logo.png"]` | > | Player poster | "Yayın başlıyor" image (`yayinbasliyor.png`) with the Mr. Bahis logo baked into the top-left corner | `.player-poster` background | > | During playback | Mr. Bahis watermark linking to `heylink.me/mrbahisguncel` (inside the `channel?id=...` iframe) | `#watermark` | > | Before the stream | Video pre-roll ad with a 5s skip button | network | > > The player config (`channel?id=zirve`, Zirve Stream template): > ``` > prerollVideo:'http://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/lookatusdoweneedu/v/zirve/mrbahispreroll.mp4' > watermarkImage:'logo.png', watermarkLink:'https://heylink.me/mrbahisguncel/' > posterImage:'yayinbasliyor.png' > ``` > If the pre-roll fails to load, the player's `PLAYER_ERROR` handler skips straight to the stream, so blocking it doesn't break playback. > > ## Steps to reproduce > 1. Open https://39macvartv.live/ (or the current number) > 2. Logo in the header and footer, icons in the top bar, logo on the player poster > 3. Press play → pre-roll ad, then the watermark on the stream > > Note: on desktop the pre-roll only plays once per browser session (sessionStorage key `preroll_watched`), so use a private window to see it again. > > ## Suggested rules > Same domain regex as the existing `[$domain=/\d+macvartv\.live/]##.footer-links`. Tested with the AdGuard Browser Extension in Firefox on 39macvartv.live: only the listed elements are hidden; the player, match list and footer text stay. The pre-roll rule is based on the player config. > > ```adblock > [$domain=/\d+macvartv\.live/]##.header-top > [$domain=/\d+macvartv\.live/]##header .logo > [$domain=/\d+macvartv\.live/]##footer img[src$="logo.png"] > [$domain=/\d+macvartv\.live/]###watermark > [$domain=/\d+macvartv\.live/]#$#.player-poster { background-image: none !important; } > ||cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/lookatusdoweneedu/v/*preroll*.mp4 > ``` > > Screenshots attached. > > GitHub: `@vurijj` ``` Username: @vurijj ``` ### Screenshots

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — fastpic.org serves its image pages behind a full-page "Your image is ready / Continue to image" interstitial, so the user must click before seeing the image; loading the reported URL reproduces it, and no existing rule removes it because the baseline only blocks the interstitial's ads and site redirects. A verified raw JS rule in CyrillicFilters/RussianFilter/sections/specific.txt (after the existing "! fastpic" block, before line 10517) auto-continues past the gate to the tokenized image page, with the interstitial gone and the image page intact. ## Rule `fastpic.org#%#(function(){var g=function(){var a=document.querySelector('main:has(h1) a[href*=".jpg.html?"]');if(!a)return;try{location.replace(a.href)}catch(e){}var m=document.createElement('meta');m.httpEquiv='refresh';m.content='0;url='+a.href;document.head.appendChild(m)};if(document.readyState==='loading'){document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded',g)}else{g()}})()` ## Policy rationale The run instruction's closing rules do not apply:⁠ the page shows no anti-adblock message, no paywall, no consent gate and no self-promotion; it is the site's own click-through interstitial page. The fix restores the user's direct access to the image instead of hiding a functional gate, so the 'never hide a gated function' rule is respected. The interstitial is not an anti-adblock wall, so no maintainer handoff is required and a rule may be generated. ## Place in the list [CyrillicFilters/RussianFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/64f5433a50ae2d70c9dd8e65cc647a9d8aa2803e/CyrillicFilters/RussianFilter/sections/specific.txt) Under the heading `! Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — Added a cosmetic rule hiding the article-body «Видео-Витрина» advertising showcase on rbc.ru:⁠ rbc.ru#⁠#⁠article ⁠> div.stroke-y:⁠has(⁠> div[⁠data-name="VideoShowcase"]⁠), placed in CyrillicFilters/RussianFilter/sections/specific.txt at line 10648 inside the existing rbc.ru group, next to the analogous ShowcaseForMarketplaces rule. Validated with apply_rule:⁠ the VTB «Мои Инвестиции» ad (disclosure «Реклама, Банк ВТБ (ПАО), 0+», cards linking to vtb.promo) that the reporter's arrow points at is hidden, page integrity intact, no residue and no remaining instances. ## Rule `rbc.ru##article > div.stroke-y:has(> div[data-name="VideoShowcase"])` ## Policy rationale The run instruction's filter policy states that ads for other companies get a rule like any other ad, including ads the site sells itself and serves from its own host or API. The reported block is a sold VTB placement disclosed as «Реклама, Банк ВТБ (ПАО), 0+». No policy rule applies to close the report:⁠ it is neither a paywall nor an anti-adblock wall nor a self-promotion-only case; the annotated target is direct-sold advertising served from rbc.ru's own markup. The report concerns website filtering, so it is open to rule generation. ## Place in the list [CyrillicFilters/RussianFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/d2226fa9fcf1a7373e198773cf2d9c7ba84703a2/CyrillicFilters/RussianFilter/sections/specific.txt) Under the heading `! NOTE: Specific rules`, before [line 10648](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/d2226fa9fcf1a7373e198773cf2d9c7ba84703a2/CyrillicFilters/RussianFilter/sections/specific.txt#L10648). ## Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reported element is the shop's own first-party cookie-consent bar (DIV.shop-consent-banner, fixed at the bottom of sklep.chemi-plast.pl); the repository's existing shared rule chemi-plast.pl#⁠#⁠.consent-banner no longer matches the site's current markup. A new domain-scoped element-hiding rule sklep.chemi-plast.pl#⁠#⁠.shop-consent-banner in AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt was validated in the reporter-profile session (bar hidden, page integrity intact, no leftover gap), so it is proposed as a new line at the top of that file's Regular rules section. ## Rule `sklep.chemi-plast.pl##.shop-consent-banner` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale No rule of the run instruction's filter policy closes this report:⁠ it is not a paywall, not an anti-adblock wall (the page's requests show no detector script and no ad-blocker message), and not a self-promotion or ad. The reported element is a cookie notice, the category the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter exists for; the filter policy states that hiding the corresponding element is sufficient in most cases. The issue is an annoyance report whose declared type and observed page content agree (bottom-fixed consent bar), so a rule may be generated. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/abb726334960dfcdd2b6e1f9dc0cf744f49a77fd/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) Under the heading `! NOTE: Regular rules`, before [line 409](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/abb726334960dfcdd2b6e1f9dc0cf744f49a77fd/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L409). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

Two candidates (repairing that selector, then a broader `:has()` rule covering all nine ad cells) hid the targeted cards in the AdGuard CLI baseline but the bound vision review rejected both — it also demands that the site's own «Сюжет»/«Доклад» special-project bandeaus be hidden and counts the free grid track beside «Главное» as residue — so the fix is a maintainer decision rather than a verified rule.

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — www⁠.backmarket.com keeps a floating app-download prompt card ("Deals so fast, only you see them", 4.7/5, App Store/Google Play badges, close X) fixed over the bottom-right of the homepage, appearing about 15 s after load — the same card as in the reporter's screenshot. No repo rule hid it, so it gets a new domain-scoped element-hiding rule in the Mobile App Banners filter's "Regular rules" section; validation showed the card visible on the baseline and hidden with the candidate, with page content intact. ## Rule `backmarket.com##div[role="dialog"][aria-labelledby="lead-collection-aria-title-id"]` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The reported defect is an in-page banner promoting the site's own mobile app, which the run instruction and AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp target; it is not a paywall and not an anti-adblock wall. No captured request shows an anti-adblock detector:⁠ the only blocked third-party loader is sdk.privacy-center.org (cookie-consent CMP), and the page content is not gated behind any action. It is not the site's self-promotion in the self-promo.txt sense of a promotional page element competing with content only by preference:⁠ it is a floating app-install prompt, the mobile-app-banner annoyance kind, and it gets a rule like any other annoyance of that kind. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/a5e8ed3f77b7722fbf5327f09fc06e1022084b40/AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt) Under the heading `! SECTION: Mobile apps - Regular rules`, before [line 4566](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/a5e8ed3f77b7722fbf5327f09fc06e1022084b40/AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt#L4566). ## Screenshots

Indeterminate — vpnjantit.com shows a site-owned anti-adblock wall (div.adb-wall, "Yo bro, hold up!") plus an inline overflow:⁠hidden scroll lock on html; hiding it alone left the page unscrollable, and the CSS-injection form that fixes both could not be certified because the site's own cookie sheet covers part of the restored hero/Quick start area in the after state. The validated-rule candidate goes to a maintainer for BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt.

## Candidate for review

`vpnjantit.com#$#html, .adb-wall { overflow: visible !important; top: 100000px !important; }`

BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt

Not verified: Two apply_rule runs of this candidate returned no failed candidate checks (the #⁠#⁠-only variant had failed page_scroll_preserved; this one passed it), adLayoutResidue absent and observedDamage empty, but visualReview stayed inconclusive both times:⁠ symptom 'unclear' and pageIntegrity 'unclear', because the site's own 'Your privacy choices' cookie sheet — present in the unfiltered baseline too — stays pinned over the lower Quick start/stats area, so the reviewer would not certify that the gated hero and Quick start content came back. The rule also relies on a user-stylesheet !important override of html's inline style, which AdGuard's compatibility notes say element hiding and CSS rules cannot do on AdGuard for Windows/Mac/Android/Linux.

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reporter marked pavlus.com's own cookie-consent bar (#⁠pavlus-consent, aria-label="Cookie consent") that stays fixed over the page; it is served from the site's HTML with no consent vendor script, so element hiding resolves it. Instead of a new line, add pavlus.com to the existing shared rule at AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt line 2158 (`…,gemini.com##div[aria-label="Cookie consent"]`), which already hides this same element on 31 other domains; validated with apply_rule (verified, symptom resolved, page integrity intact). ## Rule `pavlus.com##div[aria-label="Cookie consent"]` ## Policy rationale The defect is the site's own cookie-consent banner, which the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter exists to block:⁠ 'Purpose:⁠ this filter blocks cookie notices on web pages' and 'In most cases, simply hiding or blocking the corresponding scripts is sufficient'. No policy rule closes the report:⁠ it is not a paywall, not an anti-adblock wall, not self-promotion and not a scam page. Maintainer rule 'Shared rules:⁠ extend them':⁠ the applicable shared rule at AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt:⁠2158 is not part of a project group, so the reported domain is added to it. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/b07e256df315e3eee735bd247dfcee0de2bc9dae/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 2158](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/b07e256df315e3eee735bd247dfcee0de2bc9dae/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L2158). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

comment.body:
<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"6bfd87f67daafa2d82d1d96e0d320db4376460abb88309631576be3e8dcc8a71"} -->
The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Not reproduced — The reporter's screenshot shows a first-party anti-adblock modal from luciferdonghua.in's premium-21 plugin, which the site still ships, but with the reporter's own settings and current lists it never appears:⁠ Base Filter's existing scriptlets for this domain (antiadblock.txt:⁠2047-2048) stop the detector before its config request, so no overlay is created on the episode page, the homepage or a clicked-through episode. No rule is needed, so I recommend closing the report as not reproduced.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Policy rationale

The run instruction's filter policy states no rule that closes an anti-adblock report:⁠ it says to write a rule once the page's captured requests show the detector script, and otherwise to hand the report to a maintainer. That gate passed - the detector is verified in captured requests (inline `window.P21G` on the page, plus in the unfiltered control session `https://luciferdonghua.in/wp-admin/admin-ajax.php?action=p21_ab_config&t=...`, `premium-21/assets/js/ads/*.js` baits and the `?p21=` probe fetches) - so rule generation was allowed. No rule is generated because there is no symptom left on the reported page:⁠ complete full-page vision of the current prepared extension session reports the reporter-defined modal absent, and Base Filter's existing antiadblock rules for the domain (BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt:⁠2047-2048) are what stop the detector. The report is recommended for closing; the agent does not close it.

## Missing information

- Guidance gap:⁠ anti-adblock wall can never be present in the unfiltered control session: The outcome semantics define `already_fixed_current` as valid only when the same reporter-defined target is present in the unfiltered control session and absent with the prepared extension, and add that a target absent in both sessions must be reported as `not_reproduced`, never `already_fixed_current`. For an anti-adblock wall this test cannot discriminate:⁠ the site's detector (luciferdonghua.in, premium-21 plugin, inline `window.P21G`) only shows its overlay when it observes hidden ad bait elements, so the unfiltered control session (extension:⁠none) structurally never displays the modal even though the site still ships the detector. In this run the modal was absent in the prepared reporter-profile session because Base Filter's existing scriptlets (BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt:⁠2046-2054) abort the detector - measurable by the missing `?action=p21_ab_config` config fetch and probe requests that the control session does make - but the prescribed comparison forces the choice `not_reproduced` and gives no way to record "already covered by current list rules". A rule for how to report an anti-adblock wall that current lists already neutralize would close this gap.

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — web.de's Fairplay page shows its anti-adblock wall because the site's own CSS-based detector sees AdGuard hiding its bait containers, and the repository's existing countermeasure (web.de,gmx.net,gmx.at,gmx.ch,gmx.com#⁠$#⁠#⁠abd-container in AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/antiadblock.txt:⁠3251) no longer matches the current bait ids #⁠abd-container-sync/-async. With the selector extended to div[⁠id^="abd-container"]⁠ the page reported data-abd-detected="false" and showed its own "Vielen Dank! / Zum Login" state instead of the wall, but the vision review stayed inconclusive because web.de's financing-consent layer then covered that region, so the rule is handed to a maintainer.

## Candidate for review

`web.de,gmx.net,gmx.at,gmx.ch,gmx.com#$#div[id^="abd-container"] { display: block !important; }`

AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/antiadblock.txt

Not verified: The candidate removed the wall, but no vision review confirmed it. Phase B DOM:⁠ html[⁠data-abd-detected="true"]⁠, #⁠hero-warning displayed, #⁠hero-success display:⁠none. Phase C DOM with the tested rule web.de#⁠$#⁠html[⁠data-abd-detected]⁠, div[⁠id^="abd-container"]⁠ { display:⁠ block !important; } (same acting selector):⁠ data-abd-detected="false", #⁠hero-warning style="display:⁠none", #⁠hero-success shown — the site's own 'Vielen Dank! / Zum Login' state. Review verdict inconclusive (symptom unclear, pageIntegrity unclear) because once the detector stopped flagging the page web.de's financing-consent layer (dl.web.de permission iframe, unclickable here) rendered over the wall's region. Two later experiments for this candidate were refused before phase C (baseline_symptom_absent). This is the repository-fitting form:⁠ it extends the existing shared rule at line 3251 of the same file (domain list unchanged) so its selector matches the current bait ids #⁠abd-container-sync / #⁠abd-container-async.

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reported incorrect blocking on kaz-nakagawa.com/profile does not reproduce:⁠ with the reporter's own filters (AdGuard Base + AdGuard Mobile Ads) the page loads fully, the proxy reports zero applied rules and zero blocked requests, and no content is hidden or missing. Recommend closing; the reporter's screenshots show the AdGuard Android app home screen rather than the site, so no page-level breakage is documented.

## Policy rationale

The run instruction lists no rule that closes an incorrect-blocking report:⁠ it is not a paywall, not an anti-adblock wall, not self-promotion and not a scam page, so rule generation is allowed (no rule is needed here because nothing on the reported page is filtered). Live evidence shows the reported defect is absent on the successfully loaded reported page, so the run instruction's 'recommend closing' path applies; the agent never closes the issue, a maintainer decides.

Fallback — The page refused to load in the run browser:⁠ main document returned HTTP 403

The best unverified candidate is zpaste.net#⁠%#⁠//scriptlet('prevent-window-open') in BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt, matching the reporter's "click on button -⁠> new tab opens" defect and the repository's existing fix for the sibling paste site blizzpaste.com (#⁠popupCaptchaButton click plus prevent-window-open).

`zpaste.net#%#//scriptlet('prevent-window-open')`

BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt

The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reported account-creation overlay on the Daily Kos article could not be reproduced:⁠ five loads of the reported page with waits, reloads and a scroll to the comments never inserted the popup (its text never appeared in the DOM) and full-page vision reports it absent, while only trackers are blocked by the baseline. Recommend closing as not reproduced — the MonetizationOS surface SDK loads but renders nothing, so any vendor rule would be unverified and could break the site's own account flow.

## Policy rationale

No repository policy rule blocks this report:⁠ the reported element is the site's own account-signup prompt (self-promotion), not a paywall, paywall-adjacent content access measure, or an anti-adblock detector. Rule generation was therefore permitted; it stopped only because the defect could not be reproduced in the locked environment, not because of a policy gate.

## Missing information

- Reporter settings import cannot be applied in the locked adguard_cli session: The issue carries a reports.adguard.com settings import URL, and the run instruction says the reporter profile is reported_on_current and that only such a session may verify a rule. In the locked adguard_cli environment launch_browser rejects settings for extension "none" ("A control session (extension \⁠"none\⁠") runs no blocker and takes no \⁠"settings\⁠""), so the reporter's exact filter selection/Stealth state cannot be reproduced; the reporter-parity comparison and the reported_on_current validation session are unavailable. No fallback environment was substituted.
